meta.description: Pacha Coffee: specialty coffee seedlings, agroecological consulting, and a grower community in Misiones, Argentina.

about.title1: Argentine coffee from end to end
about.desc1: We are an Argentine company dedicated to the comprehensive development of the coffee industry.
about.desc2: We offer innovative and sustainable solutions for every stage of production, from planting to roasting and marketing specialty coffee.
about.desc3: Pacha builds its grower community throughout the province of Misiones through direct partnerships:

services.s1desc: Specialty varieties selected for the productive climates of our country.
services.s2desc: Technical and agronomic support for intensive coffee cultivation.
services.s3desc: Equipment for wet and dry cherry processing.
services.s4desc: Own-brand development with a customized roast profile.

history.title: Coffee has already grown in our land
history.lead: Argentina had long-running coffee projects in the NOA and NEA regions.
history.t1desc: In the town of Campo Grande, an estimated 300 hectares of coffee were produced.
history.t2desc: The Obispo Colombres Agricultural Experiment Station researched varieties adapted to the subtropical climate.
history.t3desc: Pacha Coffee is born with the mission of developing Argentina's specialty coffee industry from Misiones.

whynow.title: Why now?
whynow.lead: Five signals that this is the time to grow specialty coffee in Argentina.
whynow.card1desc: Regional economies are seeking new, value-added crops. Specialty coffee emerges as an alternative to diversify production.
whynow.card2desc: The zone suitable for growing coffee is shifting southward, and regions like Misiones are gaining the right conditions.
whynow.card3title: Local and international consumption on the rise
whynow.card3desc: More and more people are choosing specialty coffee, in Argentina and worldwide, and they value knowing where it comes from.
whynow.card4desc: The international price of arabica coffee is at record levels, increasing the value of every kilogram of cherry produced.
whynow.card5desc: Countries like China are increasing their specialty coffee consumption and looking for new, differentiated origins.

process.title: From seed to cherry
process.lead: Four stages that repeat and grow the community. Scroll down and watch it grow.
process.s1desc: Seedling production: each finished seedling takes between 6 and 8 months of germination.
process.s2desc: Agroecological planting design combined with care to achieve a healthy crop.
process.s3desc: In the third year after germination begins, the first harvest of ripe cherries and subsequent processing takes place.
process.s4desc: Well-maintained coffee farms last up to 50 years. Sustaining steady seedling growth allows us to expand the Pacha Community.
process.s4data: Up to 50 years of productive life
process.s3aria: Go to stage 3: Harvest and process
process.s4aria: Go to stage 4: Nurture, grow, and repeat

varieties.title: Seed curation
varieties.lead: Our seedlings are the product of a seed curation: a selection of specialty coffee varieties from geographic zones that predict the best adaptation to our country's productive climates.
varieties.quote: We guarantee traceability and quality from the very first sprout.
varieties.v1desc: A variety of Ethiopian origin that became famous in Panama. Highly floral cup with notes of jasmine and bergamot.
varieties.v2desc: Pink-cherry Bourbon. Fruity and floral cup with high sweetness and bright acidity.
varieties.v3desc: A cross between Pacas and Maragogipe, with a large bean. Complex cup and creamy body.
varieties.v4desc: A cross between Mundo Novo and Caturra. Compact and productive plant; sweet and balanced cup.
varieties.v5desc: Tall and robust plant, a cross of Tipica, Bourbon, and Timor Hybrid. Sweet and clean cup.
varieties.v6desc: A selection from the Tipica lineage, one of the foundations of arabica. Elegant, floral, and fruity cup.
varieties.v7desc: A yellow and red cherry variety. Floral and fruity cup with lively acidity.
varieties.v8desc: An Ethiopian variety cultivated in Colombia. Intense cup with red fruit notes and wine-like sweetness.
